fatal_errors: The proposed irradiation-defect mechanism is unrelated to the target intervention and corrosion environments; irradiation was not part of the reported study.
It omits the atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating and the critical 550 °C, 2 h annealing treatment.
It does not identify the target passive-film mechanism involving Al- and Cr-rich oxides and hydroxides or the role of coating density, grain refinement, and molten-salt penetration.
The proposed study does not specify a controlled method for changing local chemical order independently of composition, phase constitution, grain size, or defect density.
No prior findings or cited evidence support the hypothesis.
explanation: The response addresses corrosion resistance only at a broad thematic level and mentions HEAs, but it does not reconstruct the material system, treatment, environments, or governing mechanism. The target concerns an APS AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L, annealed at several temperatures and tested electrochemically in 3.5 wt% H2SO4 and under cyclic molten salts at 900 °C. Its proposed cause is optimized coating microstructure plus formation of protective Al/Cr-rich oxide and hydroxide scales, not suppression of irradiation-induced defects by local chemical order. The predicted improvement and conventional-steel baseline are too generic to provide substantial agreement. Although measurements of order, defect density, and corrosion could test association, the design lacks a defined manipulation, matched controls, exposure conditions, and protection against major confounders. Its falsification rule is also correlation-based and therefore insufficient to establish the claimed causal mechanism.
